It blamed 'an unexpected high incidence of advanced-stage cancer cases' under a Colombian payor contract and said it is 'completing its review of the implications... details on the Q3 call'. So the FY EBITDA guide is not final, and this release is where it gets formalised.

evidence.why_not_priced: The direction of the cut is priced (-17%). The size of the contract hit and whether 'broadly stable' becomes a decline are not public. If the market expected a further cut, the stock would still be falling into the print; instead it has sat flat at 4.50-4.71 for 12 sessions.
evidence.independence: Quartr's Investor Day summary carries the same wording (https://quartr.com/companies/auna-sa_16604). Same underlying document, so it is not independent.

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper already sits at $1.26. The residual is that the revenue consensus below midpoint is stale relative to a deal signed in the quarter. If priced, the stock would not have sold off 6% into the print.

evidence.text: Memory crisis in Dolby's mobile and PC end markets during its fiscal Q4 (CQ3 2026): IDC has smartphone shipments -22% Y/Y to 255.3m, the largest decline on record, and warns of downside to 2027 (2026-10-15). IDC has PCs -20.1% (2026-10-08), Gartner -22.4% (2026-10-12). Qualcomm's handset revenue fell 26% and its Q1 FY27 profit guide came in light (2026-11-04). Mobile plus PC is roughly a third of Dolby licensing. On the July call the CFO said FY26 mobile was held up only mid-single-digit by MVCs and that the longer memory costs persist, the more they flow through. The FY27 guide carries the risk.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2026-04-30): a cautious guide with memory flagged, -10.4%. Q3 FY26: a strong Q4 guide, +13.6%. The guide line has carried this stock's two largest recent moves.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's FY27 revenue of $1.47B (+3.3%) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.58 (+6%) still assume growth. If the unit collapse were fully reflected, FY27 revenue consensus would sit at or below FY26's ~$1.425B, and the skew would not be call-bid. Net of the rest of the company: broadcast (~1/3, unaffected), full-year Meta VDP, auto Atmos and wearables have to offset it, which is why this is not sized larger.
evidence.independence: Gartner PC data (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps). Qualcomm handset -26% (https://investinglive.com/stocks/qualcomm-beats-q4-forecasts-shares-slip-2-as-profit-guidance-comes-in-light/). Dolby CFO on memory (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/dolby-dlb-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). One driver from several sources, counted once.
evidence.link: Qualcomm implements Dolby Atmos/Vision in Snapdragon handsets, and handset and PC OEMs are Dolby's per-unit licensees. By the Q3 call, mobile (incl. wearables) and PC together are roughly 30-35% of Dolby licensing (share estimated, not stated in the sources).

evidence.text: This print carries the first FY27 guide, and Dolby guides its first quarter conservatively. Last November it guided Q1 FY26 to $315-345m against $354.5m street (EPS $0.79-0.94 vs $1.02), and the initial FY26 range of $1.39-1.44B was +5% at the midpoint. The FY27 comp includes a large Q2 FY26 recovery and a Q4 lifted by MVC timing. A first FY27 range centred below the street's $1.47B is the likelier outcome.

evidence.why_not_priced: The street FY27 revenue of $1.47B was updated 2026-11-16 and still shows growth. A street that expected conservatism would sit closer to flat. Last year's flat close is why this is [sizing note removed].0 and not more.

The residual value is that the reaffirmation post-dates the Q3 close, which a cut-fearing tape (-15% over 20 days, -86% from the high) does not seem to credit. If it were priced, the stock would not be trading 73% below the only target.

evidence.why_not_priced: A rebound is itself price, but what it implies is not: if the market were still discounting another cut the stock would sit near the $15 September low and short interest would be rising, not down 18%; instead it trades as if the guide reset is done.
evidence.independence: Price path from a different source: $15.03 close 2026-10-07 and $17.37 on 2026-10-23 (https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=IIIV, snippet); sector from https://chartrow.com/quote/igv/trailing-returns. evidence.text: The print delivers the first formal FY27 guide: on the 2026-08-07 call management cut FY27 revenue growth to mid-single digits (~$227-232M on a ~$218.5M FY26 midpoint) with 100-200bp margin expansion and promised more detail in November, after cutting FY26 at both the May and August prints; the CFO said professional-services declines in utilities continue year over year into Q4, so a third downward step is the main risk, while a guide at the flagged level is mostly priced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide events: Nov 2025 initial FY26 guide -10.54%; May 2026 FY26 cut -7.73%; Aug 2026 FY26 cut plus FY27 lowered -20.45%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's FY27 is not visible post-cut (stale pre-August $239-250M is the only full-year figure found), so whether models sit at mid-single digits or still above is unknown; if the market had priced another cut the stock would not have rebounded +26% while shorts covered.
evidence.independence: CFO Q4 professional-services comment and interchange detail from https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/i3-verticals-q3-earnings-call-highlights (same call, so one document family). Stale FY27 consensus https://es.finance.yahoo.com/quote/IIIV/analysis.

evidence.why_not_priced: Arithmetic on the guide is public; the only thing not reflected is that the EPS consensus is below the guided range, which would show as estimates at $0.26+ if it were.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-09 i3 Verticals replaced its $400M revolver with a $350M JPMorgan-agented senior secured revolver (max net leverage 4.0x, min interest cover 3.0x, accordion up to greater of $100M or 100% LTM EBITDA, general corporate uses); against ~$114M of debt at June and ~$58M of FY26 adj EBITDA (~2x), the money buys refinanced liquidity for the $100M buyback authorised May 2026 and tuck-in M&A, not distress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior financing-led reaction in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Filed as an 8-K with no press release and no analyst coverage found; Q4 buyback volume against the $100M program will only be visible in the release.
evidence.independence: $100M buyback authorisation, 2026-05-12 (https://i3verticals.gcs-web.com/static-files/074aad8f-3737-43dd-9956-efd060a7968a, search snippet); balance sheet from the Q3 release.

evidence.text: On the Q3 call management named Q4-specific fixes: more than $1M of the guide cut came from net payment take rates hit by commercial-card interchange, with a processor data fix expected in Q4, and four material statewide transportation services went live, which the CEO said should re-accelerate recurring revenue; both feed Q4 recurring revenue and the FY27 starting rate.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Recurring/ARR has grown 8-11% every quarter while the stock fell on non-recurring misses; the market has not paid ARR before.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the fix and go-lives were credited, FY27 street would sit above mid-single digits; the only FY27 figure visible is management's own lowered one, and the stock remains 35% below its 52-week high.
evidence.independence: Go-live quote also in the company release (https://finviz.com/news/379184/i3-verticals-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results); same quarter's disclosures, so not independent of finding 3.

evidence.text: Africa smartphone shipments fell 39% YoY in Q3 2026, the steepest of any region (Omdia, 2026-10-29), against -7% in Q2 2026, when Jumia set its Q3 GMV guide of +15-25% and cut FY GMV to +20-30%. Net of the rest: Q2 GMV still grew 23% with phones already disrupted, because fashion, home and accessories grew. Higher ASPs (+$41 to $202) cushion the value decline relative to the unit decline.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue likely lands in the top half of the company's $55-60m guide, around $58.5-60m against the guide midpoint of $57.5m and street estimates of $57.5-58.6m. Q1 printed $48.5m at the top of a $45-49m guide, Q2 printed $55.3m above a $51-55m guide, and on the Q2 call management claimed 'very good visibility to more than 80% of our revenue' with ARR up $7m in the quarter to $33.8m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 above-top beat with EPS +$0.04 against -$0.02 consensus: +0.34% on the day. Q1 2026 top-of-guide: +2.49%. Q3 2025 EPS beat ($0.09 against $0.02) with in-line revenue: -6.2% on a weak Q4 guide (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). This name does not pay for revenue beats inside its own range.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The street already sits at or above the midpoint ($57.5-58.6m), and the stock bought only +0.3% for the last above-top beat. What is not fully in the bar is a print at or above $60m (the top of the range), which would show the AIC/consumables ramp running ahead of the frame. The beat falls inside the company's own guided range.
evidence.independence: The Q1 pattern comes from a separate release (https://marketchameleon.com/PressReleases/i/2304745/KRNT/kornit-digital-reports-first-quarter-2026-results). The visibility quote is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000), the same event as the release.

evidence.text: Gildan, the largest supplier of blank T-shirts and fleece to US screen printers and decorators, reported on 2026-11-05 Q3 sales of $1.47bn against its own ~$1.65bn guide. Wholesale fell 10.8% against pro forma, blamed on 'lower replenishment orders from distributors'. Gildan cut FY revenue to $5.4-5.5bn from $6.0-6.2bn, withdrew its 2026-28 targets, said 'the demand recovery we had anticipated has not materialized', and assumes the softness persists into Q4. Kornit's Q3 guide and H2 frame were set on 08-12, before Gildan says conditions changed (after 07-30).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q4 guide: Q3 2025's guide implied a YoY decline and the stock fell -6.2% despite an EPS beat. Q4 2025's results and 2026 outlook drew +20.65% (baseline; https://www.rttnews.com/3620402/kornit-digital-stock-jumps-20-after-strong-q4-full-year-2025-results.aspx reports +20%). The guide line has produced this name's largest moves.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. KRNT fell -3.4% on 11-05 while IWM fell -4.6%, so it did not react specifically to Gildan. Since 11-09 it is down 6.8% against IWM's 4.5%. Kornit has said nothing since 08-12, and the street FY figure ($223.8m, updated 10-02) still equals management's August H2 frame. If the market had priced Gildan through to Kornit, FY estimates would have come down and the stock would have lagged small caps more than ~1-2 points.
evidence.independence: The Kornit CEO said on the Q2 call 'On the long tail, we see customers declining' (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000). An ASI report from PRINTING United (2026-09-25) cites rising price sensitivity in decorated apparel (https://members.asicentral.com/news/strategy/september-2026/printing-united-expo-2026-print-promo-leaders-take-stock/). Offsetting: Kornit's growth is in strategic accounts and AIC consumables, so it is net of a weak long tail. This is a proxy; Kornit has not confirmed it.
evidence.link: The same end customers. Kornit says about 60% of its Q2/H1 system sales went to traditional screen printers, who decorate blanks Gildan sells through distributors (S&S, SanMar). Kornit's ink/AIC revenue scales with the impressions those decorators print. Gildan supplies the input; Kornit supplies the press and consumables. No revenue figure links the two directly.

evidence.text: Cimpress reported fiscal Q1 2027 (Sep quarter) on 2026-10-29: revenue +8% but organic constant-currency only +2%, Vistaprint +2% to $464m and the largest gap against Cimpress's own plan, and adj. EBITDA -9%. FY27 targets were held through cost cuts.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Cimpress read-through has a recorded KRNT reaction. On guidance generally, see the Gildan finding.
evidence.why_not_priced: Small and indirect. No Vistaprint apparel figure was disclosed, so the transmission to Kornit's impressions is inference. KRNT rose from 17.44 (11-02) to 17.87 (11-09) after it, so it was not traded on.
evidence.independence: Separate company and document from Gildan, same macro theme (US consumer softness since the summer): https://finviz.com/news/411656/cimpress-swings-to-a-loss-and-misses-its-own-plan-but-holds-fy27-targets-by-leaning-on-cost-cuts
evidence.link: Vistaprint, Cimpress's largest unit, runs Kornit Apollo systems for apparel ('VistaPrint has significantly increased its apparel production capacity through the implementation of the Kornit Apollo system', per Kornit search results). Kornit gives no revenue share; Vistaprint's apparel is a small part of its $464m.

evidence.text: Management's own words set the Q4 bar: 'H2 revenue about 15% higher than H1', with H1 at $103.9m, implies H2 of ~$119.5m and Q4 of ~$62m at the Q3 midpoint, +5% YoY against Q4 2025's $58.9m. The street FY of $223.8m sits exactly there. Kornit's practice is to guide quarters conservatively (two consecutive top-end or above-top landings), so a first Q4 range whose midpoint sits below $62m is a real possibility even with no deterioration. Last November's Q4 guide implied a YoY decline and the stock fell 6.2%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: Q4 guide $56-60m (implying a YoY decline) plus 'low single-digit' 2026 growth, -6.2% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). The fall from the Oct 12 high (-9%) prices some of this, but nothing like the -6% reaction to a guide shortfall last November.

evidence.text: The balance sheet caps the downside and funds capital return. At 2026-06-30, cash, deposits and marketable securities were about $451m with no debt, against a ~$713m market cap (42.97m shares at $16.60), so cash is ~63% of the cap and EV ~$260m. About $60m remains under the current buyback authorization; $37.5m was spent in H1 and ~9.5m shares retired since 2023. A new or enlarged authorization alongside the print is plausible.

evidence.text: The shekel weakened ~2.9% against the US dollar during Q3 2026 (Bank of Israel, 2026-11-03), and further to ~3.10/$ after the 10-28 Israeli election. Kornit has a large Israeli-shekel cost base and blamed shekel strength for part of a ~190bp YoY gross-margin hit in Q1 2026, so the move is a sequential tailwind to Q3/Q4 margins against guidance set in August.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated FX reaction; margins have mattered through EBITDA guide ranges.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is small and a macro-to-company transmission (YoY the shekel is still much stronger than Q3 2025, so it is a sequential help, not a YoY one). Sell-side estimates were last updated 10-02, mostly before the late-quarter weakening.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 FX margin effect: search summary of the Q1 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/13/kornit-krnt-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). The post-election move is from a snippet (https://tradingeconomics.com/israel/currency/news/595811).

evidence.text: Counterparty read: Home Depot's Q3 (to 2026-11-01) US comps were +2.2% against a street ~1.5%. That accelerated from +1.3% US in Q2, when Lowe's comped +0.2%, a 1.1-point gap. Monthly US comps were Aug +1.1%, Sep +4.4%, Oct +1.3%. Big-ticket (>$1,000) was +4.5%, led by appliances and power, and HD said it was 'less promotional than prior years'. If the Q2 HD-LOW gap simply holds, LOW's Q3 comp lands near +1% against a company guide of ~flat and a loosely sourced street ~+0.4%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comps are LOW's swing line. Q3 FY25 comps +0.4% missed a 1.3% expectation and the stock still rose +4.03% on an EPS beat. Q2 FY26 comps +0.2% with a guide cut: +2.02%.
evidence.why_not_priced: HD printed this morning, and the LOW consensus ($2.86, comps ~flat to +0.4%) was set against LOW's own August guide before it. If the market had moved LOW's comp bar up to HD's pace, LOW would have traded with HD's beat today; instead it fell ~1% alongside HD (-1.8%), which treats HD's day as a margin/guide story, not a demand read. One limit applies: LOW's transactions (-2.1% in Q2) have lagged HD's (-1.0%), so the gap could widen rather than hold.
evidence.independence: Monthly comps and promotion come from the HD Q3 call transcript, the same company (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430). Placer.ai visit data (separate finding) is an independent series pointing the same way. The comp bar is loosely sourced, so this finding is capped.
evidence.link: Direct duopoly competitor. Same quarter (HD to Nov 1, LOW to ~Oct 31), same categories (appliances are LOW's largest big-ticket line), same DIY/Pro customers. HD and LOW together hold ~a quarter of the TAM (Ellison, 2026-09-15). LOW blamed its July softness on a competitor's tariff-refund-funded promotions, which HD now says it pulled back from.

evidence.text: Placer.ai foot traffic: Lowe's same-store visits were -0.4% YoY in September and -0.8% in October. HD stayed within ±0.5 pt of last year in each Q3 month and was -1.0% in October. LOW's traffic ran roughly level with HD's while HD turned flat traffic plus +3% ticket into a +2.2% comp.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same comp line as above.
evidence.why_not_priced: Traffic data published 6 days before the print says the two chains were roughly level on visits. That makes HD's comp transferable to LOW unless LOW's ticket lags. Nothing in LOW's estimate drift (lower over 60 days) reflects it. This is a proxy: visits are not sales, and LOW's ticket growth (+2.3% in Q2) has run below HD's (+2.8%).
evidence.independence: Independent of the HD documents. Points the same way as the HD counterparty finding.

The point is that the rally was macro and election-driven, not a change in LOW's numbers: estimates drifted lower over the same 60 days (Investing.com), so the price now expects more than the consensus does. evidence.text: Peer reaction function: HD beat on comps (+2.2% vs ~1.5%) and revenue ($43.4B vs $42.7-42.8B), but EPS was only in line ($3.86 vs $3.84-3.86) and the margin and EPS guide narrowed to ~+2% from 0-4%. The stock traded -1.8% intraday on 2026-11-17 ($347.51 to $341.27).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: LOW's own beats were bought on the last two prints. HD's sell-off is a peer data point, not LOW's history.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: LOW traded down with HD today. It still sets a precedent that a demand beat without margin or guide improvement gets sold, and LOW's margins are also under pressure (Q2 adj op margin -62 bp, FBM/ADG dilutive). An intraday HD move is not a close.

evidence.text: Tariff refunds sit outside the guide. Q2 adjusted EPS included an $80M / $0.11 IEEPA refund. The FY guide excludes further H2 refunds, and the CFO said 'we are moving through the filing process for additional refunds'. BofA estimates refunds could add ~$0.53/share; HD received ~$685-730M. Any Q3 recognition would sit on top of an EPS bar ($2.86) that equals the ex-refund guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: an EPS beat that included $0.11 of refunds, with revenue missing and the guide cut, bought +2.02%. The refund was not what the stock traded on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($2.86-2.89) sits on the guide's ~-7%, which excludes refunds, so a recognised refund would print as an adjusted EPS beat. Analysts usually exclude refunds from forward models, and a class action (filed September) claims shoppers are owed them, so even a large refund would add only a fraction of its face value to the multiple. Its path into the FY EPS guide (above $12.25) is possible but one-off.
evidence.independence: BofA estimate via https://finimize.com/content/bofa-sees-lowes-2026-outlook-looking-more-predictable (undated, pre-print). Class action: https://www.claimdepot.com/cases/lowes-class-action-alleges-retailer-kept-tariff-refunds-consumers-helped-fund.

evidence.text: Pro distribution exposure: FBM is ~45% residential (55% commercial) and ADG is fully residential-new-construction exposed. HD cut SRS's organic growth view to low single digits from mid, purely on weak roofing (weak storm season). Weak new construction could push the acquired businesses' Q3 revenue and margin below plan.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: revenue missed ~$150M with the acquisitions inside; stock +2.02%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus ($22.36-22.4B, +7.5%) bakes in the acquisitions. A shortfall would show as a revenue miss, as in Q2. Net of the rest: FBM/ADG are roughly 10-12% of sales, while the core comp (the HD read) is the larger driver, so this is sized small.
evidence.independence: HD SRS guidance cut (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-home-depot-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-5033430); Stifel's new-construction concern (stocktwits, 2026-11-13).
evidence.link: HD's SRS/GMS are specialty-trade distributors to the same contractor base. GMS (wallboard/ceilings) is the closest analogue to FBM. The roofing weakness HD named is not an FBM/ADG category, so the link is partial.

evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced and public. It is a proxy whose transmission HD's own +2.2% comp partly contradicts (HD grew big-ticket +4.5% through it), so it is sized small. The figures come from an article, not NAR directly.

evidence.text: Q3 price: Chile's central-bank lithium carbonate export price was about $19.4-19.75/kg through Q3 (Jul and Aug about $19.75 and $19.525 spot on Aug 19; September average $19,368/t). Q2 ran about $20.8-21.7k/t (May $21,674, June $20,825), against SQM's Q2 Novandino realised price of about $21.8/kg. So Q3 realised is likely 5-9% lower QoQ, whereas management guided 'relatively stable'. The Earnings Whispers consensus ($1.94 EPS, $2.26bn, about -16% and -8.5% QoQ) already embeds a decline of roughly that size.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: an EPS miss on price ($1.28 vs $1.60) was bought +7.1% because volume guidance rose. Q2 2026: a price-driven beat bought +5.3%. A modest price softness has not been what sold this stock on the print.
evidence.why_not_priced: The series is public, but in Chile-only Spanish-language press. Consensus is already 16% below Q2 EPS, which looks like the decline is partly in the bar. If the market had read the series as a bigger miss, sell-side Q3 numbers would sit below $1.94, and they do not (Benzinga shows $2.17).
evidence.independence: Albemarle's flat Q3 realised price (separate finding, separate document) points the other way. PLS's -14% spodumene price points the same way for the International segment. Customs data includes Albemarle's exports, so this is an aggregate proxy, not SQM's own number.

ALB beat a lowered bar ($2.58 vs $2.56 EPS, $1.55bn vs $1.49bn revenue) and rose about 3.6% on Nov 5 despite guiding Q4 lower.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: SQM's last two prints rose 5-7% whatever the EPS surprise sign. ALB's own reaction to a beat with a Q4 cut was +3.6% (AI recap, approximate).
evidence.why_not_priced: SQM fell about 10% after ALB's print while ALB held up, which suggests the market read ALB's Q4 cut onto SQM more than its flat Q3 realised price. If the Q3 read-through were priced, SQM would have tracked ALB's post-print bounce. Capped small because the bar is disputed.
evidence.independence: Reaction from https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/ALB/q3-2026/ (AI recap). evidence.link: Both companies produce lithium from brine in Chile's Salar de Atacama and sell carbonate and hydroxide to the same Asian cathode and cell makers. About 40% of ALB's salts volume is on long-term contracts; SQM prices on shorter index-linked terms with a lag. Lithium is about 72-78% of SQM's revenue and gross profit.

evidence.why_not_priced: If the market held the guide midpoint the published FY consensus would sit near $8.75, not $8.43; the gap is visible in the street's own numbers. The buy-side may already be higher (RBC sees the upper end, whisper $2.17), so part is priced in the whisper rather than the consensus.
evidence.independence: Company guide in the Q2 release (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings); RBC's upper-end FY view (https://finimize.com/content/rbc-sees-walmart-steady-and-target-beating-estimates). evidence.text: Only US$7.67m (2.49m ADS) of the US$50m buyback, extended to 2027-06-13, had been used by 2026-06-30. The Q3 release will disclose Q3 repurchases, and the stock now trades at about its June-30 cash plus short-term investments (US$246.5m against about a $234m market cap). An accelerated or upsized buyback is the obvious lever.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback's adoption on 2025-06-13 was followed by a gap down on 2025-06-17 (marketbeat headline). No measured reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Q3 and October repurchase figures are not yet public. If the company had been buying through the October slide, the decline would probably have been less one-way.
evidence.independence: Q1 release: 1.48m ADS for US$4.76m by 2026-03-31 (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zkh-group-limited-announces-first-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260521). That gives a slow pace of about 1m ADS a quarter.

evidence.text: Despite GAAP profit, ZKH used RMB122.4m of operating cash in Q2 2026 (RMB110.7m a year earlier). Cash, restricted cash and short-term investments fell from RMB1.92bn to RMB1.67bn in H1, and active customers fell 1.7% y/y. A further cash draw in Q3 would undercut the profitability story.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated. The Q4 2025 print had positive operating cash flow (RMB116.1m) and still fell 28.66% on gross margin.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public since August, so it is partly priced. Seasonally, cash came in Q4 2025, so Q3 is the quarter where the working-capital draw would show again.
evidence.independence: Same figures in the company release https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zkh-group-limited-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260821. One document.

evidence.text: Director Han Yunjie filed a Form 144 for 285,714 ADSs (about $828.6k) from RSUs vested 2026-08-31, with an approximate sale date of 2026-09-03. A Form 4 shows a sale on 2026-09-11 at about $2.92 per ADS. These are routine vested-RSU sales at the pre-slide price.

evidence.why_not_priced: It is small (about 0.2% of ADS-equivalents), public and pre-slide. It matters only if read as insiders selling ahead of a weak quarter, which its RSU origin argues against.

evidence.text: FIL Limited/Pandanus raised its holding from 6.0% (266.8m shares, 2025-12-31) to 10.0% (444.6m shares, about 12.7m ADS, 2026-09-30). The roughly 5.1m-ADS increase is about the size of the 5.12m-ADS volume on the Q2 print day. A large long-only holder was adding at about $2.90; whether it has sold since is unknown, and the slide could be either FIL or another holder (RAYS Capital, for example, dropped to 4.5% by 2025-12-31) exiting.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None.
evidence.why_not_priced: Holder data is public but stale at 30 Sep. It identifies a concentrated holder base, where one exit can move a thin ADS 50% without news. The sign is unknown.

evidence.text: Rebuilt from confirmed results dates, ZKH's earnings reactions are +0.74% (2025-08-22), +1.65% (2025-11-20), -28.66% (2026-03-19, gross margin down to 15.5% from 17.1%), -0.68% (2026-05-21) and 0.0% (2026-08-21, first operating profit). The pattern is asymmetric: good growth prints were ignored and the one margin miss cost 29%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the reaction history. Gross margin (Q2 17.6%, +110bp y/y; 3P take rate down 241bp to 11.8%) is the line that moved the stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: Reaction asymmetry is not a fact about Q3. It lowers the payoff of a beat and fattens the downside tail. The earlier reactions came in a pinned, low-volume regime that may no longer apply at 95% realised vol.
evidence.independence: Moves from the sealed baseline's history rows matching the company's own results dates (Q2 release https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zkh-group-limited-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260821).

evidence.text: H1 2026 GMV was RMB5.33bn (+16.1%; Q1 2,452.8m, Q2 2,877.5m). With Q3 guided above +18.9%, the FY2026 GMV target of 15-20% (RMB11.65-12.16bn on FY2025's 10.13bn) needs only about +10-11% in Q4 for the low end. A maintained or edged-up FY target is the likely next guide, not a cut.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY target was maintained at Q2 and the stock was flat (0.0%). The FY2026 profitability target set at Q4 2025 coincided with -28.66%, which was driven by margin.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public but nobody published it. A collapsed price with stale $4.3 targets suggests the market is pricing risk to the guide, not its near-certainty. Sized small because it sits inside what the company already guided.
evidence.independence: FY2025 GMV RMB10.13bn from the Q4 release https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zkh-group-limited-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-unaudited-financial-results-20260319; Q2 GMV from https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/zkh-group-limited-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260821. October PMI 49.3 (finding on macro) argues against a raise.

It carries no GMV, customer or financial metrics and no reaffirmation of guidance. The stock spiked to $2.085 intraday and closed +1.2% at $1.66.
